text:
sara: Heads-up — AcmeHealth reporting spike in p99 embeddings latency on dedicated-pool-3 since 03:00 UTC. Customer impact: search relevance degradation on two endpoints. Need fast owner + workaround timeline.

mike: assigning myself as primary for infra-side. first ask: can we confirm whether this is cold-start KV-cache misses or sustained tail? rina, can you surface p99 heatmap?

rina: quick look -> sustained tail for seq>1024. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~20% around 03:00. sending graphs: https://redwood.internal/graphs/3045 (private).

leo: customer says errors ramped after a deploy at 02:58 UTC. they saw increased retries and 502s. holding customers on an active call.

mike: @deploy-bot what rolled at 02:58?

deploy-bot: Roll event: service: model-router, image: model-router:v2026.3.5, started: 2026-03-12T02:58:12Z, owners: sara,mike

sara: that rollout touched the routing policy that added strict shard affinity for embeddings. probable cause. I can revert routing policy to allow fallback to smaller shards. Minor config change.

alex: product: need mitigation that doesn't degrade quality for >10% of queries. Can we prefer smaller batch sizes + async KV warmup instead of full fallback?

mike: plan proposal: (1) revert shard affinity to previous policy (5m rollback window) -> immediate p99 relief; (2) enable async KV prewarm for active prefixes (low risk); (3) follow-up perf test on canary. Estimate: revert + prewarm in ~30m.

rina: ops checks: autoscaler didn't trigger because pool usage stayed below threshold; we should increase burst policy but that requires config PR.

leo: customer asks for ETA and whether they'll need dedicated downtime.

sara: ETA 30–45m for the rollback and prewarm. No downtime expected. We'll communicate to AcmeHealth now.

mike: I'll open the rollback PR and tag reviewers. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/rolls/4892

sara: pinging @mike for the PR review — expedited.

mike: review done, merging now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: roll/4892 -> model-router to pool-3 (canary 10%).

rina: monitoring p99 after canary — initial improvement in canary nodes, testing full rollout.

leo: customer on call confirms canary reduced errors on their test traffic. they asked for confirmation when full rollout done.

sara: rolling remaining 90% now.

deploy-bot: Roll completed: roll/4892 -> model-router to pool-3. duration 7m.

rina: p99 dropped from 1.9s -> 320ms across pool-3. KV hit-rate rebounded.

leo: relaying to customer: they see recovery, will keep on monitoring for 2 hours. thanks.

alex: brief retrospective items: (a) add preflight perf check for routing-affinity changes; (b) add alert for KV hit-rate drop tied to p99; (c) doc quick rollback runbook.

mike: adding follow-ups to eng-platform sprint board. I'll own (a) + (b). sara will own (c).

sara: noted, will draft runbook and post PR to docs later today.

rina: also recommended: temp relax autoscaler thresholds for pool-3 while we investigate shard sizing. filing infra ticket.

leo: customer asks for a short postmortem and whether any SLA credits apply. someone from cs can follow, but engineering needs the timeline.

sara: I'll assemble timeline (deploy, detect, rollback, metrics) and share in a doc. tagging @leo for review.

mike: final note — if KV hit-rate drops recur, plan is to enable model-variant fallback (smaller sequence models) per routing policy. That would be higher quality trade-off; will design specifics in backlog.

leo: thanks; sharing with AcmeHealth.

sara: closing the incident channel once doc posted. thanks team :thumbsup:
